title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
summary: AI songs account for 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog, but it's about to be zero.
content: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
summary: A new AI-assisted proof seems to be solid, but we're not sure what it tells us.
content: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, "It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field." Read full article Comments

title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
summary: Amazon says Prime Air drones made “hundreds of thousands” of deliveries in 2026.
content: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States. The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit . After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines. “Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7. Read full article Comments

title: Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
summary: Internal memos reveal a “Code Red” overhaul and ambitious one-hour recovery goals.
content: According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters , Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide. Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote. The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report , dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
summary: Wisconsin reports 3rd measles death today; Pennsylvania reported its 9th yesterday.
content: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
summary: Study: Brewers can still use up to 50% of smoke-tainted hops without affecting beer taste and aroma.
content: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. title: Amazon discovers Falcon 9 and Ariane 6 can deliver when nobody else can
summary: Amazon has hundreds of satellites in storage waiting for rides to space.
content: A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network's build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket . The launch was an important rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the company seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA's Vulcan rocket, Amazon's primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone. The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon said, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight. Read full article Comments

title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
summary: Perseverance is having trouble transmitting to Earth. Odyssey is rapidly burning through its waning fuel supply.
content: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001 and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history. Losing its voice The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate. Read full article Comments

title: Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights
summary: Kalshi’s pause in Utah draws cheers as critics bash ads and boo insider trading.
content: Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday. It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved. Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either. Read full article Comments
